title: Capacity hedge: freelancer vs hire sensitivity (nov 2025)
content:
Executive summary:
This is a working worksheet comparing three capacity-hedge approaches for expected token demand growth across the next 12 months: (A) aggressive hiring (FTE-first), (B) blended (core hires + contractors), and (C) contractor-heavy (freelancer pool). The goal: identify the marginal cost per 1M tokens served under each approach at different pricing bands and define trigger thresholds for converting contractors into hires or enabling burst Dedicated capacity.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Time horizon: 12 months rolling (Dec 2025 -> Nov 2026)
- Base token growth (monthly): +8% compound (base), upside +16%, downside +2%
- Average token price paid by customers (hosted API): $0.004 per 1k tokens (base). Sensitivity bands: $0.003, $0.004, $0.0055, $0.007
- Average gross margin components: infra (GPU) cost per 1k tokens varies by model/quant: $0.0012 (quantized VM) to $0.0038 (full precision); we use blended $0.0022 baseline
- Ramp for new SRE/Serving hires: 3 months to full productivity; contractor ramp: 1 month
- Cost items: salary, benefits load (30%), hiring overhead (one-time $12k per hire), contractor markup (agency/freelancer platform fees ~25% on top of pay), benching and training costs accounted pro rata

Scenario layout (summary table):
Scenario / Starting FTEs / Contractors (FTE-equivalent) / Expected peak 12m tokens (B)
A - FTE-first / 48 / 6 / 18B tokens/month peak
B - Blended / 36 / 18 / 14B tokens/month peak
C - Contractor-heavy / 24 / 36 / 10B tokens/month peak

Unit economics sensitivities (select rows shown):
- Net cost per 1M tokens (in USD) under base infra cost and token price =
  A: $1,520 per 1M tokens (FTE amortized costs + infra)
  B: $1,380 per 1M tokens (mix advantage)
  C: $1,750 per 1M tokens (higher contractor premium)
- If customer price drops to $0.003 per 1k tokens: margin compression of ~25-30% across scenarios; contractor-heavy becomes loss-making earlier.
- If infra cost jumps 20% (GPU spot price spike): per-1M cost increases by ~$220 (blended) — FTE-first absorbs slightly better at scale because fixed engineering amortization lowers marginal impact.

Headcount plan (quarterly view, hires vs convert):
Columns: role | existing | hires planned (Q1) | hires planned (Q2) | contractors planned (avg) | notes
- Serving Engineers | 18 | +4 | +3 | 6 contractors | critical path — hires reduce per-token ops cost
- SRE | 8 | +2 | +1 | 2 contractors | dedicated fleet ops needed if Dedicated revenue grows
- Applied ML / Model Ops | 6 | +2 | 0 | 4 contractors | short-term fine-tune work to onboard models and quant profiles
- Support / CS (operational) | 10 | +1 | +1 | 8 contractors | seasonal ramp expected Q3
- Product / PM | 6 | 0 | +1 | 0 | strategic backlog

Contractor vs Hire economics (per-year equivalent):
- Typical senior serving contractor day rate (loaded through platform): $900/day -> annualized (220 working days) $198k equivalent; platform fees push effective cost to ~$247k.
- Senior serving FTE total cash + benefits load: base comp ~$180k + 30% load -> $234k/year, plus hiring overhead amortized ($12k over 18 months -> +$667/month).
- Breakeven tenure for a contractor vs hire (cost parity): ~9-13 months depending on platform fees and utilization. Short-term bursts (<6 months) favor contractors.

Pricing sensitivity matrix (actionable thresholds):
We map customer price per 1k tokens to recommended posture and triggers:
- >= $0.006: Accelerate FTE hiring for serving and SRE (Trigger: sustained 3-month ARR growth >25% and token volume >10B/mo). Rationale: marginal unit economics support fixed-cost amortization.
- $0.004 - $0.006: Blended posture. Use contractors for short-term spikes (>20% month-over-month), convert to hires if a sustained 6-month trend and utilization >70%.
- <= $0.0035: Contractor-heavy / defer hires, enable autoscale burst in Dedicated or cloud spot capacity to avoid fixed-cost commitments.

Trigger rules (automated watches we propose adding to Console + Finance alerts):
- Token-volume trigger: if 3-month trailing token volume exceeds 1.5x plan and projected 6-month average remains >planned capacity -> Finance flags for hire conversion (ticket JIRA:FIN-482).
- Price-slippage trigger: if realized average price per 1k tokens drops >10% vs plan for 2 consecutive months -> immediate hiring freeze and review.
- Infra-cost spike trigger: if GPU cost per 1k tokens > baseline + 15% for a month -> temporary contractor reallocation and capex request for Dedicated cost smoothing.

Capex vs Opex tilt (Dedicated capacity trade-offs):
- One-time Dedicated setup (private pool hardware procurement + infra) estimated: $3.8M for a mid-size Dedicated fleet (sufficient for 8–12B tokens/mo at target latency). This lowers per-token infra cost by ~25% at utilization >65% but increases fixed costs and requires committed revenue (Reserved capacity deals).
- Opex (cloud/spot) maintains flexibility; attractive for uncertain demand but exposes to price volatility and higher marginal cost per token.
- Recommendation: pursue a hybrid offer — reserve 50% baseline with Dedicated as a hedge only after >6 months of sustained utilization and signed reserved contracts (~12m minimum).

Stress test: downside demand (tokens flat, price compresses 20%)
- Contractor-heavy posture reduces fixed burn but still sees margin squeeze; runway extends by ~5 months vs FTE-first but risk to delivery quality and CS response times rises.
- FTE-first requires immediate cost takeouts (pause hiring, defer non-critical projects) or accelerate price increases for new enterprise customers.

Action items and open questions (notes to CFO / Head of GTM):
1) Build a simple Finance dashboard (sliding 3/6/12 month windows) with the three triggers above and per-route margin breakdown. Owner: Liam O'Neill. (Linked: JIRA:OPS-1192).
2) Validate contractor marketplace quotes for sustained pools (60–90 day engagements) — target blended discount if we commit to a batch. Owner: Sofia Ramirez.
3) Legal to review contractor SOW templates and IP retention clauses for heavy model tuning tasks (risk flagged). Owner: Noah Kim.
4) Run a short procurement RFP for Dedicated lease options (OPEX lease vs Capex buy) to compare 36-month TCO. Owner: Finance Ops.

Appendix: small worked example (sensitivity):
Base month example (simplified): 1M tokens: infra $2.20, eng amortization $0.80, ops/support $0.25, platform fees/overhead $0.10 = $3.35 per 1M tokens -> at $0.004/1k ($4.00 per 1M) gross margin ~$0.65 per 1M tokens. If price falls to $0.003/1k ($3.00 per 1M) -> loss of $0.35 per 1M tokens.

Quick decision rubric (one-pager):
- Sustained token growth + price >=$0.005 -> hire aggressively (FTE bias)
- Volatile token growth or price <=$0.0035 -> contractor-first + autoscale burst
- Mixed signals -> blended approach with 3-month watch + conversion trigger at utilization >70%

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts (informal):
- Need to align with GTM on packaging incentives to preserve price per token (enterprise commits, model variant upsell).
- Consider a small pilot: commit to a 3-month dedicated reserved capacity window tied to one large customer to verify dedicated economics before buying hardware.
- Make sure product routes show token price realized by model variant (dedupe multi-model billing).

Last lines: this sheet is a draft; numbers are illustrative. Once we get validated contractor quotes and updated infra cost curve from infra team (current ask to infra: forecast GPU hourly cost by instance class across next 6 months), we'll iterate and produce a final recommended hiring plan and approved trigger list for exec review.
